subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make a positive Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` the default for existing unset configs, and what opt-out/docs/tests are required before that ships?
rationale: The source-reproducible hardening is useful, but changing an effective sandbox Docker default can break existing workloads and changes a security boundary for upgrades.

options.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof show fresh-install, upgrade, and explicit override semantics.

options.title: Keep default unset
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior and document operator-configured `pidsLimit` as the hardening path.

options.title: Make strict cap opt-in
options.body: Use a maintainer-approved strict profile or setting if maintainers want the mitigation without changing existing unset deployments.

recommendation.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof show fresh-install, upgrade, and explicit override semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: History and CODEOWNERS evidence make steipete the strongest individual routing candidate for sandbox security-default decisions.
